subject: File control entry
notes: Rule: 'The SELECT clause shall be specified first in the file control entry. The clauses that follow the SELECT clause may appear in any order.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.2 -> OK §12.4.5.2 1)). Code: fileControlClauseGroup is `SELECT OPTIONAL? (fileName | reservedGatedWord) fileControlClauses* DOT`, and fileControlClauses is a flat alternation (assign, relative key, organization, access mode, record key, record delimiter, alternate key, file status, reserve, padding, sharing, lock mode, collating, unrecognizedClause) so both halves hold structurally: SELECT is the only possible entry opener and every following clause is order-free (ASSIGN included). Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): probe/fce/sr1order (SELECT F1 ORGANIZATION ... ACCESS MODE ... ASSIGN TO last) compiles and runs 'OK' exit 0; probe/fce/sr1nosel (`ASSIGN TO "a.dat" SELECT F1.`) is refused COBOL0001 unexpected 'ASSIGN'. No spec-derived test pins the any-order half by name; test-needed. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is stated for ALL FORMATS of the file control entry; no Annex E row touches it)]
